en: Dependent on a state that is neither unwholesome nor rootless, an unwholesome state with roots arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither unwholesome nor rootless, an indeterminate state with roots arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither unwholesome nor rootless, an indeterminate state with roots arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither-indeterminate-nor-rooted, an unwholesome state accompanied by roots arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither-wholesome-nor-rooted and neither-indeterminate-nor-rooted, an unwholesome state accompanied by roots arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is neither-wholesome-nor-rooted and neither-unwholesome-nor-rooted...
Dependent on a neutral (abyākata) conditioned (sahetuka) state, a neutral conditioned state arises by way of root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

(Abbreviated. There are six [modes] under root; six under object (*ārammaṇa*) ... pe ... three under prenascence (*purejāta*) and repetition (*āsevana*) ... pe ... three under fruition (*vipāka*) ... pe ... six under non-disappearance (*avigata*).
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor rootless, a neutral rootless state arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor rootless, a state that is indeterminate and rootless arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither indeterminate nor rootless, a state that is indeterminate and rootless arises by way of the root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor rootless and a state that is neither indeterminate nor rootless, a state that is indeterminate and rootless [arises]...

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is neither unwholesome nor rootless and a state that is neither indeterminate nor rootless, an indeterminate, rootless state arises by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor rootless and a state that is neither unwholesome nor rootless, an indeterminate, rootless state arises by way of root condition. (Abbreviated.)

With respect to cause, six; with respect to object, three ... [and so on] ... with respect to conascence, twelve ... [and so on] ... with respect to result, three ... [and so on] ... with respect to non-disappearance, twelve.
